title: Get your shopping bags out – it’s pre-order time! The 40C3 merchandise is here.
content:
We’re sure you’ve all been waiting impatiently over the last four weeks to see what the stylish 40C3 design will look like on all your favourite bits of clothing! Today we finally have the answer for you, and we’re even giving you the chance to secure some of these T-shirts and hoodies for yourselves already.

To brighten up the grey winter, we’d also like to provide you with colourful weeks’ worth of socks, 40C3 fan scarves and hats – and, if there are any little ones around, even throw in some brightly coloured kids’ T-shirts on top.

You can also avoid unpleasant surprises regarding height, length, width and other product specifications for this Congress: you’ll find a size comparison table for 40C3 and many other hacker events from recent years in the Merch Size Comparison Guide.

And, as always, the small print: you have until 20 December to place your orders, as we cannot guarantee that payments will be processed after this date. Please only place an order if you have a way of actually collecting the goods. This means that you either have a ticket for 40C3, or someone with a ticket can collect the goods for you upon presentation of the collection code.

title: Call for Interpreters: Translate 40C3!
content:
Planning for Congress, unsure what to do there, interested in applying your impressive language skills? If you are multilingual and fluent in German, English and maybe other languages, please consider joining the interpreters team, c3lingo.

We interpret ALL talks on the five main stages live and in real time. German talks are interpreted into English, and vice versa. Our work is streamed to the Internet and transmitted as audio-only streams in the halls, and recordings are published on media.ccc.de. We have another channel where we interpret into more languages, this is transmitted and published in the same way.

title: 40C3: Hackertours
content:
TL;DR: 17 tours to exciting places in Hamburg, available now in the Hackertours shop!

There is a world outside of Congress at 40C3, too: the Hackertours have prepared 17 tours to exciting places in Hamburg. You can book them in the Hackertours shop right now.

This year, we are looking up to the stars: the Planetarium Hamburg has four shows for us, from the journey of the Voyager probes and The Future of the Universe to full-dome music shows with Pink Floyd’s The Dark Side of the Moon and Imagine Dragons. If you prefer real telescopes, visit the historic domes and the library of the Hamburg Observatory in Bergedorf.

Also new: a peek behind the scenes of the DESY Computing Centre, with tape library, HPC cluster, storage, and the cooling, power, and network that keep it all running. And the European XFEL in Schenefeld opens its doors to us again: we descend five floors underground into the experiment hall of the X-ray laser that generates up to 27,000 X-ray flashes per second.
snippet: TL;DR: 17 tours to exciting places in Hamburg, available now in the Hackertours shop!
sourceDescription: Recent content on CCC Event Blog

title: Your first Congress? Chaos Mentors are here for you at 40C3!
content:
Interested mentors and mentees can register on our Chaos Mentors platform until November 30, 2026, at 23:59 UTC+1.

Chaos Mentors are back at the Chaos Communication Congress this year – and things are even more exciting this time around: we are moving to a brand-new venue! For us as experienced mentors, this means we will also be doing a bit of exploring, hunting for the best shortcuts, and figuring out where the quickest Mate refill stations are hidden. In short: it is the ultimate opportunity to explore this new space together and join us in making it our own!

Rest assured, though: while the floor plans might be a fresh adventure for all of us, we are still your seasoned experts when it comes to everything that truly defines Congress. We know how to tame the overwhelming schedule, how the community ticks, and how to pace yourself amidst all the creative buzz. After all, we have already mastered the “Chaos” part – navigating a few new hallways together will be a breeze.

We are looking forward to welcoming many newcomers ready to experience the colorful, fascinating chaos of Congress for the very first time – maybe even with you!
snippet: Interested mentors and mentees can register on our Chaos Mentors platform until November 30, 2026, at 23:59 UTC+1.
sourceDescription: Recent content on CCC Event Blog

title: 40C3: Call for Angels
content:
Once again this year, the angels are Citizens of Congress. They are the many thousands of hard-working volunteers who help to shape Congress and make it an even more wonderful place for everyone. This is our model for society and shows how we work together to put on a fantastic Congress.

Whether you’re joining us for the first time or have been with us for quite a while, you always have the chance to support us and take a peek behind the curtains of Congress. The range of tasks on offer is vast: from the relaxed job of manning a remote emergency exit with another Angel to the hectic task of serving drinks at the Main Bar, where you’ll have lots of interaction with other people.

If you’d like to help out, please register via the Engelsystem. Once you’ve arrived at Congress, please feel free to pop into (Pre-)Heaven or one of the satellite venues at the two entrances. There, you’ll receive your Angel badge and can then sign up for shifts to help with the upcoming tasks. Alternatively, you’ll find Heaven on the upper floor of Hall B1. Please bring your lanyard for your Angel badge. The Engel-Guide contains way more information about being an angel.

title: Haecksen Workshops Call for Participation
content:
Once again, Haecksen will be expanding the Congress programme with a workshop room!

Haecksen are a group of FLINTA people interested in technology, aiming to promote intersectional feminist perspectives within the hacker scene and STEM professions.

The Call for Participation for the Haecksen workshop programme is already live, so now is the time to submit your concepts for workshops, discussion groups or evening events.

Especially FLINTA persons and marginalised beings are invited to submit their workshop ideas. For your inspiration, here are the four tracks:

  • Diversity & Inclusion
  • Skill Sharing
  • Community & Activism
  • After Hours

    • The full CfP with all info and the submission form is available on Pretalx.

    The deadline for submissions is Wednesday, 25 November 2026, at 11:42 p.m. (Europe/Berlin).
snippet: Once again, Haecksen will be expanding the Congress programme with a workshop room!

title: Click your way to happiness at halfnarp
content:
Want to get a sneak peek at what’s happening on the stages at 40C3 this year? Would you even like to help make the stage program as smooth as possible and ensure we know which talks shouldn’t be scheduled at the same time?

This year, the five main talk stages will be spread across two sections of the venue. So even as we’re putting together the schedule, we need to make sure we don’t trip over each other’s feet later when we’re slipping back and forth between the halls.

So go ahead, scroll through the talks that have already been confirmed, click on everything you want to see, and show us which ones shouldn’t be scheduled at the same time or placed too close to each other.

title: 40C3 - Call for Heralds
content:
This year, the Heralds will once again guide the 40C3 program. In response to feedback from previous years, we’ve made a few small changes.

Want to join the Herald team? Email 40c3-heralds@cccv.de by December 15 with the following information:

  • Which Herald category you see yourself in (mentor, experienced Herald, or Herald mentee)
  • A link to a recording of you moderating (if available)
  • Languages spoken (German/English/French)
  • Your preferred topics or tracks (e.g. Security, Hardware, Politics & Society, Art & Beauty)
  • Your availability (day, morning, afternoon, evening, or night)

    • The Heralds guide the stage program at 40C3. They introduce speakers, keep talks on schedule, and moderate Q&A sessions. They also escort speakers to their rooms.

    To become a Herald, you must attend the introductory meeting on Day 0. The time and room will be announced later.

    There are three types of Heralds:

    Experienced Heralds who can also serve as mentors

    If you have experience moderating on larger stages (audiences of more than 500), this role may be right for you. You should also be willing to help a new generation of mentees take their first steps on the big stages.

    Experienced Heralds without mentees
snippet: This year, the Heralds will once again guide the 40C3 program. In response to feedback from previous years, we’ve made a few small changes.
sourceDescription: Recent content on CCC Event Blog

title: 40C3: So it is. So it shall look.
content:
Congress is rapidly approaching. How it turns out in the end depends entirely on how you turn it into a wonderfully wild hackers’ carnival and spruce up yourselves, your websites, assemblies, and fingernails. That’s why now is the time to get us all visually ready for this – for us, the most beautiful – time of the year. And it’s going to be beautiful!

This year, mcgraw has gone all out for you and crafted a Chaos Identity that’s multi-layered and thought-provoking, lovingly reflecting all creatures, and at the same time breathtakingly beautiful. Something we can really be proud of.

To give you a sneak peek at what 40C3 will look like, we’re presenting the full package today. On the info pages, you’ll find a detailed DIY kit with all the bells and whistles: colors, shapes, and fonts to customize, decorate, and look your best at the Congress.

title: 40C3: Call for Assemblies
content:
tl;dr: Register your assembly before 23 November 2026, 23:42 CET (UTC+0100) on the Hub.

A reboot does you good: this also and in particular applies to the assembly areas of the Chaos Communication Congress. The Hamburg exhibition halls offers more space for assemblies and projects — in contrast to the Congress Center. However, a bit of imagination is required to give this space that certain something. Help us make this space something very special.

Show the world what you do in your hackspaces and what moves you. Work together on projects, look for and find like-minded people, meet old and new friends. Be Model Citizens — or the exact opposite.

  • Please do not bring large structures without consulting the Assembly Team first. Rule of thumb: the larger the structure, the earlier you should consult us. Larger structures will be subject to a building inspection.
  • Register your assembly before 23 November 2026, 23:42 CET (UTC+0100) on the Hub and tell us about your plans.
  • Any questions? Send an e-mail to 40c3-assemblies@cccv.de.
  • If you need help with storage/logistics or have questions about material deliveries, please contact us at the address listed above.
snippet: tl;dr: Register your assembly before 23 November 2026, 23:42 CET (UTC+0100) on the Hub.
sourceDescription: Recent content on CCC Event Blog

title: Mostly Harmless
content:
Mostly Harmless is the first big event by Magrathea Laboratories.

Mostly Harmless – MHL in short – is a weekend for everyone that likes to try stuff, create, discuss or wants to make new things together. In 2026 our slogan is “Follständig Harmlos – experimentieren, diskutieren und hacken“, which translates to something like “Mostly Harmless – experimenting, discussions and hacking“ with a deliberate typo in the first word.

“Follständig“ connects the “Mostly Harmless“ theme from Douglas Adams’ Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy, with a regional Carnival greeting, “Fölsch foll“. The event venue is in Hünfeld, the Konrad Zuse city (where Zuse lived for most of his life) – a fitting place for a weekend between tech, creativity, and new ideas.

Whether you’re linked to a hackspace, IT, culture, or maker scene, or simply curious: At MHL we want to get together to learn and build while discovering new perspectives.
snippet: is the first big event by Magrathea Laboratories.

title: CCC invites all model citizens to 40C3
content:
The word is on the street: the Chaos Computer Club is hosting 40C3 from 27 to 30 December 2026 – Europe’s biggest hacker party, conference and platform for technology, society and civil liberties. We understand the Congress to be a huge shared stage and therefore invite you to help shape it. The Call for Participation for talks, the entertainment programme, art, punk and music opens today.

Everything is getting bigger, more colourful and more beautiful. Following our moving to the Hamburg Exhibition halls, there is once again plenty of space for creative ideas. Obviously, we want to make the most of this new space, which is why we are inviting all galactic beings to the 40th Chaos Communication Congress from 27 to 30 December 2026.

title: FediDay 2026
content:
• 2 ½ day conference around the Fediverse
  • talks, workshops, panels, party
  • 11–13 September, Berlin

    • The Fediverse is not one platform – it’s a universe of its own. It contains microblogging and longreads, videoclips and images, podcasts and music and much much more. It is running on a diversity of software, operated by different communities but all connected by open protocols. What holds it together isn’t a company or a business model — it’s a shared idea about how we communicate online and who holds the control of that.

    We are convinced that a decentralised and free network is the best way to establish a sustainable alternative to Big Tech. This is the only way to enable democratic exchange without being dependent on platforms controlled by profit-driven monopolists, which use algorithmically generated timelines to serve us adverts, promote right-wing baiting or hide content they find objectionable.

title: NooK 2026: Call for Participation
content:
Moin! The “Nights of Open Knowledge” (NooK) 2026 will take place on 20–⁠21 November at the Audimax (the largest lecture hall) of the University of Lübeck. The Call for Participation for NooK 2026 is now open. You can submit proposals for talks, workshops, stalls, or meetups. Submissions are open until 28 September.

We would be delighted if you could bring topics that fascinate you to the event and share your knowledge and skills. Whether you’ve engaged with a topic through a hobby, a club, at university, at work, or through political activism, we cordially invite you to submit your proposal. Your talk or workshop can cover almost any field: from current research, archaeology, and board games to climate, computer science, medicine, journalism, digital independence, open source, and lifestyle. Almost anything goes!

NooK is especially a place for you if you haven’t had much experience with giving talks yet. We would love to motivate you to share your ideas. We also welcome artistic contributions to enrich our foyer; please use the “stall” submission form for this.
